description: UMH role classification for each of the 13 production stack layers, per Trinity app. Defines what UMH owns vs what each app owns.

role_taxonomy.owner: UMH directly owns and operates this layer for the app
role_taxonomy.orchestrator: UMH coordinates and sequences actions across apps for this layer
role_taxonomy.observer: UMH monitors and reports on this layer but does not control it
role_taxonomy.policy_governance: UMH defines policies and gates that the app must satisfy
role_taxonomy.integration_layer: UMH provides integration points that the app connects to
role_taxonomy.no_direct_role: UMH has no involvement in this layer for this app

apps.integration_boundary: None — EOS frontend is fully app-owned. UMH does not serve or control EOS UI.
None — CreatorOS frontend is fully app-owned.
None — LyfeOS frontend is fully app-owned.
EOS owns its API. UMH may provide integration endpoints for cross-app intelligence, agent orchestration, and governance queries. Integration is via defined API contracts, not direct substrate access.
apps.data_flow_if_any: EOS → UMH: governance queries, work packet status. UMH → EOS: agent results, intelligence insights (future).
blocked_actions: No direct substrate access from EOS backend

apps.integration_boundary: Same as EOS — CreatorOS owns its API. UMH integration via contracts.
Same pattern. NOVA AI coaching may route through UMH intelligence layer (future).
apps.data_flow_if_any: LyfeOS → UMH: coaching requests (future). UMH → LyfeOS: AI responses via model router (future).

apps.integration_boundary: EOS owns its database. UMH may observe schema health and migration status but does not access EOS data directly.
apps.data_flow_if_any: UMH observes migration status and schema health metrics.
blocked_actions: UMH never queries EOS database directly

apps.integration_boundary: Same — CreatorOS owns its database.
blocked_actions: UMH never queries CreatorOS database directly

apps.integration_boundary: Same — LyfeOS owns its database.
blocked_actions: UMH never queries LyfeOS database directly

apps.integration_boundary: EOS owns its auth. UMH sets the policy (Clerk required) and gates deployment readiness on auth compliance.
apps.data_flow_if_any: UMH governance checks auth status before approving deployment work packets.
blocked_actions: Cannot deploy without Clerk migration complete

apps.integration_boundary: Same — UMH policy requires auth bypass elimination before any deployment.
apps.data_flow_if_any: UMH governance blocks deployment until comparePasswords vulnerability eliminated.
blocked_actions: CANNOT deploy until auth bypass fixed

apps.integration_boundary: Same — UMH policy requires Clerk standardization.
apps.data_flow_if_any: UMH governance tracks auth migration status.

apps.integration_boundary: EOS owns its deployment config. UMH orchestrates deployment sequencing, readiness gate verification, and rollback decisions.
apps.data_flow_if_any: UMH → EOS: deployment approval. EOS → UMH: deployment status.
blocked_actions: Cannot deploy without readiness gate clearance

apps.integration_boundary: Same pattern.
blocked_actions: Cannot deploy without auth fix AND readiness gate

apps.integration_boundary: Same pattern. LyfeOS already deployed — migration to Fly.io is the deployment action.
blocked_actions: Migration to Fly.io requires readiness gate

apps.integration_boundary: EOS cloud compute is managed services (Fly.io, Neon, Clerk). UMH has no compute role for EOS.
Same.
Same.
EOS owns its GitHub repo and CI/CD. UMH orchestrates source truth reconciliation (production truth promotion, source strategy decisions).
apps.data_flow_if_any: UMH tracks source truth status per app. UMH production truth promotion includes source reconciliation.
blocked_actions: Source strategy (DEC-145-001) must be resolved before CI/CD setup

apps.integration_boundary: CreatorOS owns its repo. UMH observes source health.
Same — LyfeOS has clean source state.
EOS owns security implementation. UMH defines security policy and gates deployment on security compliance.
apps.data_flow_if_any: UMH governance verifies security requirements before deployment approval.

UMH sets rate limiting policy (from OS Platform Standard v2). App implements.

EOS owns its recovery. UMH orchestrates cross-app incident response and coordinates rollback decisions.

summary.note: UMH never owns a Trinity app layer. It orchestrates (deployment, recovery, source truth), governs (auth, security, rate limiting policy), observes (database health, error tracking, source state), and provides integration points (API contracts). App ownership is always with the app.
summary.key_principle: UMH owns orchestration, governance, and cross-app intelligence. Each app owns its own product, code, data, and infrastructure.
